correctness.rationale: Shift u=x-K/2 and complete the logistic square: u'=-u^2/K-P(K/2+u)y, y'=[P(K/2+u)-P(K/2)]y. Positive y makes u strictly decreasing. If u<=0 it reaches x=0 in finite time by Riccati comparison. On a hypothetical global u>0 trajectory, u->0, ∫u² dt<=Ku(0), and ∫u dt=∞, since a finite ∫u would leave y bounded below away from zero and force a crossing. z=u²/y has exactly z'=-2P(r+u)u-[2u/K+P(r+u)-P(r)]z. For alpha<=2, the bracket is bounded below by -Cu², so its integrating factor stays positive and the integral ∫P u diverges, forcing z negative: contradiction. For alpha>2, on y=cu², c<(alpha-2)/(2KP(r)), the outward derivative is negative near u=0, while u' is between two negative multiples of u², proving a nonempty positively invariant wedge with no finite-time boundary contact. Rational derivative alpha=-4K²(bK+4)/(aK²+2bK+4)² and explicit parameter triples verified symbolically; the theorem is for all positive initial predator data on the exact critical parameter surface, not trajectories continued through negative prey densities.
